name: Jacky Cheung
description:
'''Jacky Cheung Hok-yau''' (born 10 July 1961) is a Hong Kong singer and actor. Cheung is one of the [[Four Heavenly Kings (Hong Kong)|Four Heavenly Kings]] of [[Cantopop]] and is often dubbed as the "[[Honorific nicknames in popular music|God of Songs]]." His first album ''Smile'' (1985) sold over 300,000 copies in Hong Kong and his second album ''Amour'' (1986) sold over 400,000 copies, earning a multi-platinum certification from [[International Federation of the Phonographic Industry|IFPI]] Hong Kong. After a period of declining sales in the late 1980s, [[The Goodbye Kiss (album)|''The Goodbye Kiss'']] (1993) sold over 4,000,000 copies, becoming one of the best-selling albums in Asia. In 1995, his albums sales exceeded 5,000,000 copies, making him the second highest-selling artist in the world that year, behind Michael Jackson. He is the [[List of best-selling albums in Taiwan|best-selling music artist of all time in Taiwan]] and Hong Kong, and has sold over 60 million albums worldwide. Cheung has embarked on [[List of Jacky Cheung live performances|ten concert tours]], with the [[Jacky Cheung 1/2 Century Tour|1/2 Century World Tour]] (2010–2012) setting a [[Guinness World Records|Guinness World Record]] for the largest audience for a live act in twelve months. [[A Classic Tour]] (2016–2019) became one of the [[List of most-attended concert tours|most-attended concert tours of all time]], drawing over 4.5 million people. His accolades include the [[Billboard Music Awards|''Billboard'' Music Award]] for Most Popular Asian Singer in 1994, and the [[World Music Awards|World Music Award]] for the World's Best-Selling Asian Artist in 1996. In 1999, Cheung was honored by [[Junior Chamber International]] as one of the Ten Outstanding Young People in the World. In 2000, he was inducted into the Superstars Hall of Fame of the 1990s by [[Universal Music Group|Universal Music]]. 

As an actor, Cheung starred in films such as ''[[Devoted to You (film)|Devoted to You]]'' (1986), ''[[Where's Officer Tuba?]]'' (1986)'','' ''[[As Tears Go By (film)|As Tears Go By]]'' (1988), and ''[[The Swordsman (1990 film)|The Swordsman]]'' (1990).
